subject: takahe bird
title: This Bird Was Declared Extinct for 50 Years. Then a Doctor Found It

scenes.text: This bird was officially extinct for fifty years. It was hiding in the mountains.
The takahē is a flightless New Zealand bird, chicken-sized, with a huge red beak.
By eighteen ninety-eight, only four had ever been found. Everyone assumed it was gone.
In nineteen forty-eight, a doctor named Geoffrey Orbell searched Fiordland's remote Murchison Mountains.
In a hidden valley, his team caught two live takahē in a net.
Today there are more than five hundred. Back from extinct, twice.

description:
The takahē was believed extinct twice, in 1850 and again from 1898, until Dr Geoffrey Orbell's team rediscovered it in Fiordland's Murchison Mountains on 20 November 1948.
After decades of conservation work, the population passed 500, with an estimated 529 birds in the last full count.
What other animal do you think is still out there, waiting to be found?
first_comment: The lake where they were found is now called Lake Orbell, after the doctor. Which extinct animal would you most want rediscovered?
